turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay, thanks for jumping on so fast. [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2], [PERSON_3] is on with us from support. [PERSON_1], you wanted to walk us through what you found.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes. I was doing a routine audit Friday afternoon, pulling transcripts from the central scheduling queue, and I found a call where the patient's information was sitting right there in the transcript, plain as day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. Can you read me what's exposed?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I'll read it exactly as it appears. Patient name [PATIENT_1], date of birth [DOB_1], MRN [MRN_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's a scheduler call. She called in to move an appointment.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: There's more. The agent read back the callback number [PHONE_1], and her home address, [ADDRESS_1], Nashville.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. I'm writing this down as you go.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Spoken dates of birth and MRNs are coming through in the transcripts completely unredacted. Card numbers get masked, but those don't.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: [PERSON_1], how many calls are we talking about, just this one?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I've spot-checked about forty so far and found four with the same pattern. I stopped there because I wanted to get on this call before I went further.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's helpful. Can I ask a couple of questions about the configuration while we're here?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Please.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Which redaction settings are currently turned on for the account? Is it the standard profile or something custom?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: As far as I know it's whatever we set up at implementation. I haven't touched it. I can pull it up if you tell me where to look.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll send you the exact path after this call. And just to confirm on my side, card numbers are being masked correctly?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yes. We tested that ourselves, the payment calls show the card as masked. That part's fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good. So the masking is working for card data but not for the spoken identifiers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: That's the shape of it. And I'll say this now while everyone's here. We need to be able to choose which identifiers get redacted, and lock that setting so a regional admin can't turn it off.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Understood. I'm not going to guess at what's possible on that, I want to take it to the product team and come back with something concrete.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I appreciate that, but I need more than concrete eventually. We have a BAA. This is reportable if it goes wider.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I know. And I'm sorry this happened. Let's figure out what we can do right now to stop the bleeding, then work the rest.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Can we turn transcripts off for the scheduling queue in the meantime?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's a config change, so I don't want to promise it on this call. Let me look at what's available for that queue specifically and get back to you today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Today would be good. I've got agents on that queue around the clock.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Understood. I'll also want to know whether the calls in question came in through the main tracking number or a campaign number, so I can scope how far back this goes.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Most of our scheduling calls come through the main line. The campaign numbers are more for the clinics' outreach.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can send you the four call IDs I found. Should I send them to you directly, [PERSON_3]?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yes, that works. Send them to me and I'll attach them to the ticket.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: [PERSON_1], who else at Meridian knows about this so far?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Just [PERSON_2] and our general counsel. I haven't told the clinic leads yet.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. I'll keep this tight on our side. [PERSON_3], me, and my director, that's it for now.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. I don't want this bouncing around.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Here's what I can commit to. By end of day tomorrow you'll have a written summary from me of what we know and what we're doing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: By Thursday I'll have an answer from product on the redaction controls. And [PERSON_3] will have the transcript question answered today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll confirm that in the ticket before I sign off today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: And the exposed records? Do we need to do anything with those transcripts?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I'll ask about options for those specific calls in the same conversation. I don't want to tell you something today that I can't stand behind.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's fair. I'd rather you come back straight with us than guess.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Agreed. One more thing, and this is procedural. Any communication about this needs to come to me and to [PERSON_2], not to the clinic managers.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Noted. [PERSON_3], anything else you need from them before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Just the call IDs and confirmation of the queue name. I have the rest.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'll send the queue name right after this.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. [PERSON_1], thank you for bringing it to us quickly. I know this isn't how you wanted to spend a Monday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, it isn't. But here we are. I'll watch for your summary tomorrow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: You'll have it. Talk soon.
